items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, after Lucky Roberts and after Billy Fowler. I got in Horace Henderson's band.

ctx.x: So this was after Lucky Roberts?

Yeah, after Lucky Roberts and after Billy Fowler. I got in Horace Henderson's band. And we were working a place called Dunbar Palace, it was a place where people get -- well, it was a dance in the evening, you could all the sorority clubs give them parties and balls there. dance, you know. And you give--for, And the band is a beautiful band. In fact, we had the same music that his brother had. Horace would steal his brother's music but Horace was a beautiful arranger. And he had all this beautiful music. And the…

So we played, stayed together for quite some time. Until about 1933 or something like that, '34. Now in the meantime, I'd met a man and he asked me (inaudible). So I said, yes, if you play me a certain salary. And I was there. The big solo was to play "Dinah," and "St. Louis Blues" and things like that.

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: There's a guy that was a trumpet player [Jacques] in my band named Jack Butler.

ctx.x: I had ten men. Excellent band. I think this happend, if I'm not mistaken, before I went into the Dunbar Palace. Right, because we did an audition for -- you had to make a few auditions, you know, to get the job. And of course, the night club operator didn't think anything about having another band over in the corner fighting after

you played your time. And they would judge, and you had to actually sell yourself for the job, you know, and -- but I had some good guys. They were New York musicians and were more or less experienced. It didn't take us long. They were good readers, these guys, and in fact, I've got a picture of a group that I had (inaudible) at Dunbar. They were guys that (inaudible) you evidently have heard some of these fellas. There's a guy that was a trumpet player [Jacques] in my band named Jack Butler. He went to Europe,…
